prompt: I deployed my React SPA to Walrus Sites but direct links to /dashboard return 404. How do I fix it?
expected_output: Adds a routes section to ws-resources.json mapping /* to /index.html and redeploys with site-builder deploy.
expectations: Shows the routes section in ws-resources.json with /* mapped to /index.html
Mentions redeploying with site-builder deploy for the change to apply
Explains that routes are client-side routing rules stored on the site object

prompt: Can a Walrus Site return an HTTP 301 from an old URL to a new page?
expected_output: Yes: the redirects field in ws-resources.json defines server-side HTTP redirects with location and status_code, including glob patterns; the portal evaluates them before fetching a resource.
expectations: Shows the redirects field in ws-resources.json with location and status_code
Mentions that the portal evaluates redirects before looking up the resource
Does NOT claim Walrus Sites cannot do HTTP redirects

prompt: Every GitHub Actions deploy of my Walrus Site creates a brand new site object instead of updating the existing one. Why?
expected_output: ws-resources.json, which records the site object ID, is not committed, so CI's fresh checkout has no object ID; commit it (or pass --object-id).
expectations: Identifies the missing ws-resources.json / object_id in the CI checkout as the cause
Recommends committing ws-resources.json to the repository
Mentions --object-id as the way to target an existing site explicitly
